strands.name: Number and Operations
strands.description: Counting, place value, and the four operations, built from the NCERD Number and Operations strand.

objectives.description: Count to and across 100, forwards and backwards, from any given number
Represent and partition numbers to 20 using concrete materials and pictorial representations
Count by 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s, forward and backward, to 100
Read, write and compare numbers to 100, exploring to 200
Read, write and order numbers to 1,000 using place value
Add and subtract 2- and 3-digit numbers using a range of strategies
Recognise, compare and simplify fractions with small denominators
Read, write, order and compare numbers to 10,000
Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 10 times tables
Recognise decimal place value and add simple fractions with the same denominator
Identify and write factors of 1, 2, 3 and 4 digit numbers
Write numbers in expanded notation, e.g. 3,047 = 3 x 1,000 + 0 x 100 + 4 x 10 + 7 x 1
Find fractions and percentages of amounts, and convert between simple fractions and percentages
Describe, identify and write sets, including equal and equivalent sets and subsets, using set notation
Find prime factors of a number and use them to find the LCD (lowest common denominator) of fractions
Simplify ratios, share a quantity in a given ratio, and round decimals to a given place

strands.name: Patterns and Relations
strands.description: Number patterns, equality and early algebraic reasoning, from the NCERD Patterns and Relations strand.

objectives.description: Identify, describe, extend and create repeating patterns with two or three elements
Given a number, identify one more and one less
Understand that different combinations of numbers can represent the same value
Represent equalities using a pan balance and other concrete materials to explore the equals sign
Identify, describe and extend increasing and decreasing number patterns
Demonstrate an understanding of equality using addition and subtraction to 1,000
Identify and describe situations with constant or varying rates of change
Represent, describe and extend patterns and relationships using charts and tables
Continue and describe increasing and decreasing patterns involving whole numbers, fractions and decimals
Represent a given pattern using a table of values and predict subsequent terms
Use number patterns to find the lowest common multiple (LCM) and greatest common factor (GCF) of two numbers
Solve problems involving single-variable, one-step equations

strands.name: Geometry
strands.description: Shape, position and transformation, from the NCERD Geometry strand.

objectives.description: Sort 2-D shapes and 3-D objects using one attribute, and explain the sorting rule
Describe the relative position of objects using the language of position, e.g. above, below, beside
Describe, compare and sort 2-D shapes and 3-D objects according to the number of sides, edges and faces
Describe and identify lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes
Identify and describe the properties of quadrilaterals and triangles
Describe and perform single transformations (slides, flips and turns) of 2-D shapes
Describe position on a simple coordinate grid and use compass directions
Identify, describe and classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or straight
Describe and construct 3-D objects, including edges, faces and vertices, and identify nets of common solids
Plot and translate coordinates on a grid, and describe turns using compass directions
Measure and classify angles using a protractor, and identify complementary and supplementary angles
Describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations of 2-D shapes on a grid
Plot coordinates in all four quadrants and describe translations using compass directions
Identify and describe properties of prisms, pyramids and other 3-D solids, including their nets
Determine the perimeter and area of regular and composite shapes
Describe and perform combinations of translations and rotations using coordinates and compass directions

strands.name: Measurement
strands.description: Length, mass, capacity, time and money, from the NCERD Measurement strand.

objectives.description: Compare and order objects by length, mass and capacity using direct comparison
Tell time to the hour and half hour using an analogue clock
Estimate and measure length, mass and capacity using non-standard and standard units
Tell time to the nearest five minutes, and relate days, weeks and months on a calendar
Measure and record length, mass and capacity using standard metric units
Solve problems involving the addition and subtraction of money in Guyana dollars
Convert between related metric units of length, mass and capacity, e.g. cm to m, g to kg
Determine the perimeter of regular and irregular polygons
Determine the area of rectangles and composite shapes made from rectangles
Solve problems involving elapsed time, including conversions between seconds, minutes, hours and days
Solve real-world problems involving length, mass, capacity, money and time, applying the four operations
Determine the volume of rectangular prisms using cubic units and a formula

strands.name: Data Analysis and Probability
strands.description: Collecting, displaying and interpreting data, from the NCERD Data Analysis and Probability strand.

objectives.description: Collect, sort and organise objects into a simple pictograph, and answer questions about the data
Describe events using the language of chance, e.g. certain, possible, impossible
Construct and interpret bar graphs and pictographs with a many-to-one correspondence
Determine and compare the likelihood of simple events using the language of chance
Collect, organise and display data in tally charts, frequency tables and bar graphs
Determine the range and mode of a small set of data
Construct and interpret double bar graphs, and draw conclusions from displayed data
Determine the probability of a simple event as a fraction of equally likely outcomes
Construct and interpret line graphs to display data that changes over time
Determine the mean, median, mode and range of a data set
Construct and interpret pie charts and use them to compare parts of a whole
Solve problems that involve interpreting and comparing data from more than one graph
